notes: A 6 gal compressor on a 120 V, 60 Hz single-phase supply with an approximate cut-in of 120 psig and cut-out of 150 psig. The manual has no parts list, so parts are named by function, and its cover says oil-free pump while another copy calls the pump maintenance-free.

gaps: The manual has no parts list; it points to servicenet.porter-cable.com for parts, which refused connection, so no part numbers are given.

The two copies differ on the pump wording: the Internet Archive copy's cover says oil-free pump and the ToolsID copy's says maintenance-free pump; the oil_lube absent claim rests on the Internet Archive cover only.
The manual names no motor type or horsepower; the motor sits under the motor_ac key only as the nearest fit, not as a claim of induction type.
The 120/60 supply and the 15 A minimum branch circuit in the spec table are the compressor's, not stated for the motor, so no v or a is set on the motor; they are in the notes.

The ToolsID copy's tank-life notice (remove the tank from service by the year on its label) is not in the Internet Archive copy's English text, so it is left out; the 22.7 L figure is only on the translated pages, so it is left out too.
The manual does not say how many cylinders the pump has or whether it is single or two stage.
method: Delta Porter-Cable C2002 air compressor instruction manual N003568 (oil-free pump), PDF on the Internet Archive (item manualsonline-id-36f6e225-8e4d-4977-9ed6-02df28b6a514), read as text with the research tool.
Pages used: 1 cover, 7 specifications, 9 power cord, 10 controls and components, 11 motor overload protector, drain valve, check valve and break-in procedure.
A ToolsID copy (images.toolsid.com) was opened to compare; it is a mirror with a different cover wording and is not used as a source.
The Porter-Cable service site (servicenet.porter-cable.com) refused connection and was not used; retailer parts pages for the C2002 type numbers were skipped.

comps.spec: Air compressor pump: bore 1.875 in, stroke 1.250 in; 3.7 SCFM at 40 psig and 2.6 SCFM at 90 psig, tested per ISO 1217 (specification table)
Electric motor that the pressure switch starts and stops
Motor overload protector, automatic reset thermal type: shuts the motor off if it overheats and restarts once it has cooled
Pressure switch: approximate cut-in 120 psig and cut-out 150 psig (specification table)
On/Off switch that feeds power to the pressure switch in the On position
Safety valve: if the pressure switch does not shut the compressor off, it pops out at a factory-set pressure slightly above the cut-out setting
Drain valve at the base of the air tank, used to drain condensation after each use; opened counter-clockwise during the break-in procedure
Check valve: open while the compressor runs so air enters the tank, closes at cut-out to hold tank pressure; replacing it or the pump needs the break-in procedure
Regulator with a knob that sets the outlet pressure (clockwise increases it)
Tank pressure gauge: shows the reserve pressure in the tank
Outlet pressure gauge: shows the pressure after the regulator
Cooling-system fan that blows air out through the vent holes
Power cord and plug with a grounding pin; the manual says cord repairs need a qualified electrician
